text.en: Meena looked at an onion peel under the microscope and saw neat little boxes. "Those are cells," said her teacher, "and groups of similar cells make tissues."

A tissue is an organised group of cells that work together for a function. It can include several types of cells and material around them. Plant tissues are of two kinds. Meristematic tissues are made of cells that keep dividing and cause growth, found at the tips of roots and shoots. In plants, specialised permanent tissues carry out particular functions. Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals, and phloem transports sugars from sources to places that use or store them.
Animal tissues are of four main types. Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines organs. Connective tissue joins and supports parts, as in blood, bone and cartilage. Muscular tissue moves the body by contracting. Nervous tissue carries messages as impulses.
Cells multiply by cell division. In mitosis one cell divides to make two identical cells for growth and repair, and in meiosis the chromosome number is halved to make gametes.

Begin with a cell, then zoom out to a tissue, an organ and an organ system. A leaf is an organ formed from several tissues, each contributing to the work of the leaf.
A meristem is a region of dividing cells. At a root or shoot tip, an apical meristem helps the plant grow longer.
The lateral meristems of many plants help stems and roots grow thicker. In grasses, intercalary growth regions can occur near the base of leaves or around nodes.

board.text: Intercalary → growth near bases or nodes

text.en: Cells in many permanent tissues have taken on specialised jobs. Some mature cells retain the ability to divide under certain conditions. Tissue names describe their typical roles.
Parenchyma is a simple tissue. Some of its cells store food. In green tissues, parenchyma with chloroplasts can take part in photosynthesis.
Collenchyma gives flexible support to growing parts. Sclerenchyma has thick walls that often provide harder support, as in some fibres and seed coverings.
The epidermis covers the surface of many young plant parts. In a leaf, pairs of guard cells control openings called stomata. Those openings affect gas exchange and water loss.

board.text: Epidermis covers · guard cells control openings

text.en: Xylem and phloem are complex tissues, made from multiple kinds of cells. Xylem helps link root water uptake with the leaves and also supports parts of the plant.
A mature leaf that provides sugar is a source. A growing root or developing fruit can be a sink. Phloem transport connects the source with the sink.
Animal tissues include epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissue. An organ can contain all four working together.
Epithelial cells form sheets over surfaces or along cavities. Squamous cells are flat, cuboidal cells are more box-shaped and columnar cells are taller.
A thin epithelial layer can aid exchange. A thicker, layered epithelium can protect a surface. Compare the shape and arrangement before proposing a job.

board.text: Structure can support exchange or protection

text.en: Connective tissue often has material between its cells. Bone has a hard supporting matrix, cartilage is more flexible and blood has a liquid matrix called plasma.

board.text: Connective matrix can be hard, flexible or liquid

text.en: Tendons connect muscles to bones. Ligaments connect bones to other bones at joints. Keep the attachment points in view to remember the distinction.
Skeletal muscle often helps move bones under voluntary control. Smooth muscle contracts in organs such as the intestine. Cardiac muscle contracts in the heart.
A neuron receives and sends signals. A long branch called the axon carries signals away from its cell body in the simplified diagram. Other cells help support nervous tissue.

board.text: Neuron sends signals · support cells help the tissue

text.en: Imagine moving a finger. Nervous tissue carries signals, skeletal muscle contracts, connective tissues transmit force and the skin’s epithelium covers the surface.

board.text: One movement involves several tissue types

text.en: Mitosis separates copied chromosomes into two nuclei. Cell division can then produce two daughter cells with the same chromosome number as the starting cell.
Plants can use mitotic cell division for growth at their tips. Animal tissues can use it to replace some worn cells. A division and a later change in the cell’s role are different processes.

board.text: Growth and repair use cell division

text.en: Meiosis has two nuclear divisions after one round of DNA copying. In the simple model, it produces cells with half the starting chromosome number.
In animals, meiosis is part of gamete formation. Fertilisation brings two sets of chromosomes together again. Compare this with mitosis, which maintains the chromosome number.
Finish by describing one tissue from its structure and job. Then name one other tissue that works with it in the same organ. This links the cell scale with the job of the whole organ.

board.text: Link structure, function and the whole organ

problem.en: A growing root receives sugars made in a mature leaf. Which tissue carries them, and which tissue supplies water to the leaf?

text.en: Trace sugar from the mature leaf to the growing root.

why.en: Phloem connects a sugar source with a place that uses or stores it.

text.en: Trace water and dissolved minerals from the root toward the leaf.

why.en: Xylem is the main pathway for this transport.

prompt.en: A friend says Muscular tissue carries messages to the brain. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Muscular tissue contracts to move parts.

points.en: Tissues are groups of cells organised to work together.
Mitosis generally preserves chromosome number. Meiosis reduces it.
